projects.title: NewBrain
projects.overview: October 28, 2026: NewBrain's original 11,914-parameter, 42-token core completed a fixed weighted Original12 intervention. Total remained 2/12: two previously wrong substantive answers became correct but both previously correct abstentions were lost, and no new checkpoint was adopted. A separate Oct 27 NB21 original-core synthetic study improved direct symbolic answers from 0/12 to 11/12, reordered from 0/12 to 4/12, with all 48 frozen/trained records matching after restart. Neither proves broad conversation or Original12 improvement.
projects.status: LATEST OCTOBER 29: Actual47 verified local numerical mathematics (988 completed objective/gradient evaluations, 480 parameter differences, 18 feature differences). On a fixed check-only first-prefix comparison, normalized routing effect on centered logits rose from about 5.04e-8 to 0.11136 L2, with NO change to top-token choice and NO free-answer test. Actual49 reused original teaching and Original12 assessment: legacy control 2/12 (0/10 factual; 2/2 missing-information), normalized routing candidate 1/12 (0/10 factual; 1/2 missing-information); candidate REJECTED and checkpoint NOT adopted. Actual51 DIFFERENT 12-question development set: unadapted 0/12, routing-only 0/12, full adaptation 2/12; all correct full answers were missing-information controls, factual answers 0/10. Predeclared success criterion FAILED. Actual52 complete-answer and held-out-composition diagnostic SOURCE IMPLEMENTED / REVIEWED ONLY, UNRUN. Accepted protected Original12 remains 2/12. EARLIER Oct28 original weighted 2/12 with 2 new substantive answers but 2 older abstentions lost; Oct28 routing-only development 0/12 answerable, 4/12 missing-information before/after. Separate Oct27 NB21 synthetic learning 11/12 direct and 4/12 reordered, not Original12. All original failed 0/12 candidates and previous NB14/15/16 historical findings remain preserved in dated reports.
projects.how: Controlled experimental tests use frozen prompts, source-scoped scoring, saved complete generated answers, unchanged no-teaching controls and separate process-reload checks. On October 23 the no-teach execution saved 20 unscored responses, and this consumed test must not be repeated. A separate read-only scorer with fresh provenance and appropriate authorization is needed before drawing accuracy conclusions; then future new admissions may run matched replay/no-replay learning, unfamiliar-combination transfer, and restart retention. Lower loss alone does not qualify a learning gain. The newest paper shortlist includes numerical-gradient correction, raw-history retrieval baselines, N-gram patch writing, harness/skill learning, within/across-episode memory and visual grounding. These are externally reported research ideas, not NewBrain implementations. The varied-form comparison NB15 and the OLD replay coverage comparison NB16 were both completed October 27 and both failed their stated transfer targets. The next proposed task is to qualify the accepted checkpoint, source, vocabulary and counters using disjoint public controls before attempting to transfer a training change, without tuning on protected Original12 cases. After Oct 28 zero-net-gain, a proposed fresh matched experiment should assess both new symbolic acquisition and preservation of unknown-answer abstention without inspecting protected Original12 answers.
projects.technical: Oct29 Actual47 evaluated 988 native mathematical objectives/gradients, 480 parameter and 18 feature finite differences. After one check-only update per product form, the original routing logit effect had L2 ~5.0397e-8 (legacy) vs ~0.1113574 (unit-RMS normalized); top token remained unchanged. Actual49 matched only routing-parameter updates for 384 steps per arm using unchanged original 24-row teaching, 2,304 presentations, frozen base roles and value weight 4. Exact true-EOS complete answers were reproduced across process restart, but normalized arm regressed Original12 to 1/12. Actual51 compared routing-only against all ten existing parameter groups with 384 matched updates, same normalization, four-value weighting, clipping and independent 12-question context-conditioned development evaluation. Complete answer traces repeated in a distinct process; only the two missing-information controls succeeded under full adaptation. No new parameters, tokenizer or architecture, no replacement checkpoint. Next full-answer versus held-out-context diagnostic has static-reviewed source ONLY, no execution. Older tiny reference learner NB14 improved some direct/alternate results but is a separate 8,343-parameter model, not accepted Original12.
projects.evidence: Reviewed October 29 evidence: Actual47 direct CPU math qualification; numerical route-logit L2 ~0.11136 versus ~5.04e-8, no free answers. Actual49 original protected Original12 legacy routing 2/12 versus normalized 1/12 after equal 384-update exposures; 24 primary answers matched 24 restart answers exactly, no checkpoint adopted. Actual51 separate context-conditioned development study: unadapted 0/12, routing 0/12, full 2/12; both correct were missing-information controls; all 36 primary answers matched a distinct-process 36-answer restart. Source52 source review only, checks/results unrun. Public details: newbrain.html#newbrain-mathematics-and-learning-2026-10-29 and updates.html#newbrain-avatar-results-2026-10-29. Previous October 28 and 27 reports, NB14/15/16 findings, numerical checks, and negative retention runs remain in archived dated research records; historical notes are retained.
projects.privacy: NewBrain is local/private research rather than a visitor service. Iris receives only reviewed public summaries and cannot open private curricula, raw questions, model weights, identities, histories, media, local runtime state or unpublished experiment records. The Kira Labs website does not send Iris questions into NewBrain.
projects.limits: As of October 29, stronger local route-logit influence did not produce correct complete factual answers. The normalized Original12 candidate lost one old correct missing-information answer (1/12); full adaptation on a separate development set produced only two correct missing-information controls (2/12), no factual answers. Actual49 used previously seen teaching/assessment content, not novel generalization; Actual51 lacks complete historical per-row exclusion. No production state, Qwen parity, general cognitive success, independent scientific replication, delayed semantic retention or model-based autonomous person is established. Original12 accepted score remains 2/12; source52 unrun. Raw protected questions, keys, state and personal data remain private. Historic limits remain in dated reports.
projects.cost: No public NewBrain product or price exists. Research budgets propose shared lab/compute, student help and optional higher-memory GPU resources; hardware is not a substitute for model diagnostics. All figures are planning estimates, not measured minimum requirements.

projects.title: IdeaForge
projects.overview: IdeaForge is a local-first invention research and project-planning workspace. It turns an idea into goals, subsystems, research questions, reference choices and staged prototype plans while distinguishing available technology, experimental work and fictional or undemonstrated goals.
projects.status: October 21 review: IdeaForge retains its local-first engineering project, equipment, optional voice and prototype-planning components. A new exact project-folder identity fix has passed 14 isolated CPU and injected UI/source checks, including duplicate names, strict numeric IDs, concurrent folder reservations, selection and refresh. These checks do not qualify full native-GUI or model behavior.
projects.how: Start with an idea and define its goals, known engineering facts and unknowns. Organize subsystems, compare research and reference images, and build a staged prototype plan. The research queue and recurring watch operate while the app is open. The automatic geometry path currently makes parametric enclosures only when required dimensions are supplied; other shapes need custom CAD. An optional PyBullet runner takes an existing URDF, rather than automatically validating an entire invention.
projects.technical: The documented setup is Windows with Python 3.11 or newer, a prepared Python environment and local Ollama with qwen3.5:9b for chat. qwen3-vl:8b is optional for image analysis. OpenSCAD can export enclosure STL when separately installed; PyBullet is a separate optional tool. Voice needs an explicitly built .NET/System.Speech helper, an installed English recognizer, a suitable Windows voice and a working microphone. The newer project indexing path atomically reserves independent numeric folders and prevents unknown eight-digit IDs from falling back to fuzzy display-name lookup. It can leave an incomplete folder if a later multi-file write fails; full transactions and hostile filesystem races are not solved.
projects.evidence: A scoped review tested actual copied project/index/main UI code with 14 fresh synthetic checks covering numeric IDs, duplicate display names, six concurrent creators, collisions, traversal-like titles treated only as labels, and exact UI path selection. This supports stable project identity in those fixtures, not fully integrated app reliability, crash recovery, native Tk behavior, speech recognition, actual Qwen answers or fabrication safety. Earlier tests and adverse records remain.
projects.privacy: Project files, equipment records and history are stored locally, and the default model endpoint is local. Research is online: outgoing searches can include the project name, subsystem questions and saved engineering facts. IdeaForge should not be described as fully offline or as guaranteeing that invention details never leave the computer. Voice records no raw microphone audio, but recognized questions enter ordinary chat/project records. Iris cannot access those records.
projects.limits: Automatic CAD is limited to the documented parametric enclosure path with known dimensions. Other geometry remains custom CAD or TBD. OpenSCAD output, a mesh check or an optional existing-URDF simulation does not certify an invention’s safety, manufacturability or real-world function. Speculative goals and unsupported technology must stay labeled.
projects.cost: These notes establish no public IdeaForge price, packaged installer or reuse-license grant. Its documented local models and optional CAD/simulation tools require their own setup and computing resources. Iris itself has no AI-service subscription or per-question model charge.

projects.title: Humanoid Researcher
projects.overview: Humanoid Researcher is a local-first research library and candidate-design workspace for humanoid robotics and body subsystems. It organizes source material and proposed designs while keeping verified facts, candidates and unresolved details separate.
projects.status: As of October 17, 2026, Humanoid Researcher collects source-attributed research by body subsystem, supports local chat and opt-in Windows voice, and prepares candidate parts and equipment notes. Main-branch updates through October 2 do not establish a complete, validated robot.
projects.how: Collect and categorize research, retain source metadata, and compare possible body subsystems against recorded requirements and equipment. Candidate tools can propose revisions, BOM and fastener schedules, assembly documentation, supplier searches and diagrammatic blueprint sheets. Keep VERIFIED, CANDIDATE and TBD distinct. Supplier links and lower prices do not prove compatibility or authorize substitution.
projects.technical: The app is Windows-oriented Python 3.11 or newer. Chat defaults to local Ollama qwen3.5:9b; screenshot interpretation needs optional qwen3-vl:8b. Collection uses online sources. A daily Windows scan is separately opt-in. Optional Windows voice starts off and requires the speech helper, installed recognizer and voice, plus a microphone. Embodiment modes are planning architectures, not deployed hardware.
projects.evidence: Implementation and stated boundaries were reviewed October 3, 2026; this is not a fresh end-to-end run or robotics certification. Compatibility scoring is a heuristic over recorded interfaces and ratings. It does not establish mechanical, electrical or thermal safety. Blueprint views remain diagrammatic placeholders unless verified geometry exists. CAD-derived views, physics/electrical/thermal validation and a fabrication-ready release gate remain roadmap work.
projects.privacy: Research, media, library and equipment records remain local in the documented setup and are not website content. Source collection and supplier searches use online services. Paper and image reuse still depends on original rights. The daily scan is opt-in and voice is initially off. Iris sees only this public summary and cannot retrieve local equipment records or private project memories.
projects.limits: This is a research and candidate-design tool, not an autonomous safe robot builder. Heuristic compatibility scores, conceptual BOMs and diagrammatic blueprints are not engineering certification or fabrication-ready geometry. No demonstrated mind uploading, consciousness transfer, deployed robot or active qualified NewBrain integration is claimed.
projects.cost: No public Humanoid Researcher price, packaged consumer release or reuse-license grant is established by these notes. Local models, speech components and engineering tools need separate setup. Iris’s free browser-only answers do not certify or fund hardware construction.

A named candidate profile does not prove an active skilled expert. The early Synthetic Robert route is independent of NewBrain's experimental learning model. Full physiology, adaptive sensory cognition, functional internal organs, virtual Voice Box and Evelyn public installation remain unverified. projects.title: BlueBook
projects.overview: BlueBook is a local-first workspace for investigating UAP and anomalous-phenomena records while preserving attribution and uncertainty. It organizes cases, sources and reported descriptions without treating an unresolved report as proof of an extraordinary explanation.
projects.status: BlueBook 0.2 retains sourced UAP cases, 2D maps and 3D globe, program records, attributed entity descriptions, AI reconstruction prompts, provisional discovery and opt-in Windows speech. Its latest source changes were October 2; no extraordinary claims are verified.
projects.how: Read attributed case records, inspect source material and reported descriptions, and compare related cases. Competing-hypothesis templates list assumptions, missing evidence and falsifiable checks. They assign no probability or winner and cannot promote a hypothesis into a finding. Automatic discovery periodically checks configured feeds and archive pages while the app runs; discovered records remain provisional until reviewed.
projects.technical: BlueBook uses Python 3.11 or newer and a local server. Local Ollama qwen3.5:9b is optional because deterministic routing remains available. Reconstruction prompts work without an image backend; rendering requires a separately configured local AUTOMATIC1111-compatible API. Hands-free uses the server computer’s microphone and installed Windows speech components, starts off, stops when the page is hidden/closed, and allows only one app or tab to use the shared speech engine.
projects.evidence: Implementation and boundaries were reviewed October 3, 2026, not freshly validated end to end. A government document establishes that a record exists, not that every interpretation is true. Witness and news claims remain attributed; unresolved does not mean extraterrestrial, and descriptor similarity does not prove identity. AI reconstructions are visualizations based on reported descriptions, not photographs or evidence. Hypotheses have no assigned probability or winner.
projects.privacy: User media and generated images stay in local folders in the documented setup. Online archive/news requests, external map tiles and CDN scripts mean the application is not fully offline. Optional hands-free requires same-computer local access and permission to use that computer’s microphone. Iris cannot read BlueBook’s local case notes, media or chat history.
projects.limits: BlueBook does not prove extraterrestrial life or turn a reported entity into a verified identity. AI reconstructions are not evidence. The record library is incomplete, and full timeline or relationship-graph UI remains architectural planning rather than shipped tabs. Missing evidence, competing explanations and source reliability must remain visible.
projects.cost: No public BlueBook price, packaged release or reuse-license grant is verified in these notes. Optional local models and image generation need separately configured tools and computing resources. Iris itself uses no paid AI service or model subscription.

projects.title: Aster Workstation
projects.overview: Aster is a local-first personal workstation companion with her own identity, explicit memories and an intended future NewBrain reasoning core, designed to support research and practical computer tasks.
projects.status: Current October 21 snapshot: Aster remains a research-stage local workstation companion with bounded modules. A separate opt-in five-initialization retention experiment tested a fixed empirical-gradient weight-protection penalty against matched replay. The fixed experiment found no incremental penalty benefit. It does not enable a production brain, live NewBrain replacement or verified autonomous desktop work.
projects.evidence: In the frozen tiny synthetic retention experiment, every tested arm finished old-task 6/6, new-task 6/6 and eight wording checks 8/8 for each of five repeated initializations. Even new-only training retained old cases, so the task did not expose forgetting; it cannot establish that replay or the extra penalty prevents forgetting. The additional penalty failed its prespecified benefit gate and was not adopted. Paired checks, saved-state restoration and cross-environment tests were scoped engineering evidence, not novel real-world language evaluation.
projects.limits: No penalty benefit was established: the toy task had perfect endpoints even without replay and exposed no forgetting. The test does not demonstrate continual-learning transfer, general language competence, a working NewBrain backend, unrestricted desktop action, live webcam understanding or generated persona conversation.
projects.how: This research progresses through documented, limited software and engineering tasks. Proposed goals must be tested separately before they are described as working capabilities.
projects.technical: Aster's opt-in test used a byte-pinned small token model, five fixed initializations, matched replay/penalty arms, 384 old warmup and 192 subsequent updates per arm. The parameter-protection term uses a diagonal squared-gradient importance proxy, not verified biological synapses or exact Fisher geometry. It incurred two additional parameter-sized arrays and descriptive overhead. The study does not modify the main NewBrain repository or Aster production behavior.
projects.privacy: Iris reports reviewed public summaries only. She cannot access private accounts, local project data or confidential research communications.
projects.cost: This research is not a public paid service. Any future deployment and equipment requirements are not yet established.

projects.title: Person Creator
projects.overview: Person Creator is the public name chosen by Kira Labs on October 24, 2026 for the Kira World research previously called Temporary Creator or Temporary AI Creator. It was renamed because not every person it aims to create is temporary: it is meant for distinct experts, companions and characters, some created for short sessions and others intended to continue with separate identities, interests, memories and relationships. The tool remains a staged source-aware profile-creation experiment, not a working one-click person generator. Evelyn Hart began as an AI/technology specialist in this research and is now separately being developed for continuing conversations and a future free public demonstration.
projects.status: As of October 24, 2026, the public product name is Person Creator (formerly Temporary Creator/Temporary AI Creator); the new title is an owner naming decision, not a newly passed test. Existing prototype source profiles, historical and fictional interpretation boundaries, documented technical preparation and the October 22 illustrated mind/body/voice design remain the underlying evidence. Complete automated individual creation, live conversation, independently accepted persistent memory, Avatar Builder handoff, original voice and a public installer are not yet verified. Evelyn's short original voice greeting was subsequently approved and publicly published on October 24. This is a distinct audio milestone, not a verified Person Creator end-to-end expert voice or finished tool. The older generator remains available in a version of Video Studio as synthetic-person work moves to a new planned voice approach.
projects.how: Person Creator is intended to start with the individual's approved identity and knowledge sources, character history, personality, goals and consent rules. An individual could be classified as temporary for a bounded task or as continuing for a longer-lived companion; those are properties of the person, not of the creator. The design prepares appearance and expression requirements for Avatar Builder and voice characteristics for the current generator. Only independent, successful end-to-end tests would establish working mind/body/voice integration. Future authorized digital-twin research requires explicit consent and is not a working one-click digital clone.
projects.technical: The name was changed publicly October 24, 2026. Earlier code directories, source files and video titles may still use TemporaryAI or Temporary Creator as legacy identifiers; this is intentional for backward compatibility, not a second application. Candidate identity/source pack and review stages exist. Integration with the local current generator, Avatar Builder and NewBrain requires separate runtime qualification. A simulated voice box/vocal folds is future research; no physical or simulated vocal organ is operating as a released Person Creator component.
projects.evidence: Existing controlled profiles include Emily Carter (coding), Jessica Hale (robotics), Ryan Hale, Laura Mitchell and Sarah Bennett, with historical and fan-made studies such as late-1893 H. H. Holmes and Peter Parker clearly distinguished from real people and licensed public characters. Evelyn Hart emerged from an earlier specialist-profile workflow. These historical experiments predate the Person Creator name and do not prove live unrestricted dialogue, independent learning, memory continuity or full automatic person construction. The October 24 rename itself is documented on the website and development timeline.
projects.privacy: Each intended individual needs separate permissions, source attribution, identity and memory records. Temporary or continuing is a profile/continuity distinction, not consent to reuse personal information. A digital-twin study requires explicit authorization for any person's audio, photos, likeness, interviews and stories. Private owner recordings and personal memories are not accessible to the website or Iris. Fan and historic portrayals require proper rights and provenance labels.
projects.limits: Person Creator is a name for research in progress, not proof of a finished, sentient, self-sustaining or independently knowledgeable person. A completed one-click expert, persistent digital companion, natural avatar, cloned identity, voice box, integrated NewBrain brain and public release have not been established. The October 24 naming change introduced no new tested runtime ability.
projects.cost: No public Person Creator installer, live creation service or price exists. Source/profile prototypes and future implementation studies are under development. An individual being temporary or continuing does not imply a published pricing tier.

projects.title: Evelyn Hart
projects.overview: Evelyn Hart is a developing synthetic individual with an approved original synthetic voice and an actual 58.125-second October 25 recorded demonstration: four local Qwen-generated replies in her approved voice accompany offline scripted head, eye, blink and jaw motion. The video uses a licensed developmental base, not the final Evelyn body. Her independently authored original V9 and V10 heads were rendered October 26 but REJECTED. The local 30-publication starter library is staged, not read or distributed, and real live conversation and visitor memory are not qualified.
projects.status: As of October 29, the original A45 blank head (14 views) and A44 cropped torso controls (12 total views) remain visually rejected. They are not Evelyn's accepted face or body. The previously approved original 3.04-second greeting and the separately recorded 58.125-second four-reply video on a licensed developmental head remain public. The isolated generic original eyeball was accepted for appearance but is not fitted to Evelyn; selected eye color blue does not mean eye integration. Evelyn has no complete original anatomical body, interactive live audio loop, verified mature visitor continuity, new runtime/installer or physiology. The 30-title library is staged and not read. The planned virtual Voice Box is research only; new proportional correction code is unrun.
projects.how: Evelyn's intended app separates continuing identity, permitted visitor memories, Qwen-backed conversation, source-aware facts and a personal library under Windows Documents/Kira Labs/Library. The 30 selected publications are ordinary files in subject subfolders, not an on-demand ZIP archive; actual in-app reading and page-linked recall require runtime tests. The earlier 22-title stage remains preserved. Two original primers cover Star Trek technology and representations of AI/synthetic characters in film and TV, but these are written research references, not watched films or personally learned material. NewBrain remains a separate research backend and has not replaced Qwen.
projects.technical: The approved Evelyn recording is a 145,964-byte mono PCM16 24-kHz WAV, approximately 3.04 seconds, and has identical Git blob SHA e7b6a2ac646dbcab4098a261ba9dc23725597e75 in the retained private and public copies. The approved greeting can be played and downloaded at evelyn-hart.html#evelyn-original-voice-approved-2026-10-24. The earlier Qwen3-TTS 13-file preparation check and recorder-wrapper rejection remain a separate failed preflight. A repeated independent synthesis trial with different text, voice consistency after restart, full speaker-to-face synchronization and complete interactive conversation need fresh runtime evidence. The reviewed app work also includes source-level Add Document checks, a 30-publication library candidate with 11 PDFs and 19 text editions, 163-bone body export/parity checks, planned privacy overlays and before-action recording rules; none of these source reviews alone establishes reading, motion or installation. Internet-first installation, licensed books, private-memory protection and disconnect/restart behavior remain release gates.
projects.evidence: The 30-publication local candidate preserves the earlier 22 books: TECHNICAL — Dive into Deep Learning, Elements of Robotics, Full Circle Magazine Issue 137, Think Data Structures, Think Python, Think Java, Think C++, Think Stats, Think Bayes, Think DSP and Think Complexity. VARIED — Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Tartuffe, On the Origin of Species, The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin, Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, The Time Machine, Frankenstein, The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes, Etiquette by Emily Post, A Tale of Two Cities and The Complete Works of William Shakespeare. Eight later additions are Pride and Prejudice, Jane Eyre, The Picture of Dorian Gray, Dracula, Passages from the Life of a Philosopher, Sketch of the Analytical Engine (1843) with Ada Lovelace's Notes A–G, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman and Notes on Nursing. This is 13 technical and 17 varied publications, each not read or released. Two prepared AI/film-and-television primers are separate. Source-license, historical-context and noncommercial limitations remain. Separately, a genuine, owner-approved Evelyn voice greeting is now recorded and publicly playable on Evelyn's site; the library assembly did not cause or validate that voice, nor does the short recording prove live conversation, synchronized movement or user installation. The later actual 58.125-second video demonstrates four locally generated replies voiced in approved original synthetic speech with offline scripted head/eye movement; it is not a live autonomous performance. The distinct public-censored five-second sitting clip uses a licensed rig. The Kira Labs original head V9 clay views were generated but rejected, not approved. A generic original eyeball milestone was separately inspected, but it does not upgrade Evelyn's rejected V9/V10 head, demonstrate blinking/gaze or provide individual eye color selection. Evelyn narrates the public 3-minute 12-second Kira Labs fundraising film at https://kiralabs.org/fundraising-film.html. This is approved synthetic voiceover, not a new facial lip-sync, living-memory or live conversation result.
projects.limits: The approved 3.04-second greeting and recorded four-reply video do not establish live arbitrary dialogue, natural facial synchronization, autonomously controlled body movement, mature visitor memory or a final installable product. Both original V9 and V10 heads failed visual approval; the licensed stand-in is not the accepted Evelyn body. Thirty staged reading titles remain unread and unqualified for publication. The voice generator preview is unsigned and not comprehensively GUI/clean-machine validated.
projects.privacy: Separate authorized visitor profiles and permission-scoped memory are planned, but real John-to-Cindy-to-John recall and post-restart privacy tests have not passed. Her private books, visitor conversations, source recordings, personal preferences and reference images must stay local/private and out of downloadable release and Iris. Only rights-reviewed and permitted books could be included in a later public release. Someone saying a known name or resembling a person must not automatically unlock private records.
projects.cost: Robert intends Evelyn's standalone Windows demonstration to be free to the public once it is properly tested and safe to distribute. No installer or launch date is yet available. Included books/media require rights review, and the original 22 locally assembled publications are not an approved redistribution bundle.

founder_education.title: Robert McMurrer · Education

His coursework included business, marketing, communication and organizational management. The marketing certificate is an undergraduate certificate, not a second degree.
